hints: Compare each dashed line to the solid line in two ways: how steep it is at the start (rate) and where it finishes (final total product).
Remember an enzyme speeds up a reaction by lowering activation energy, but it cannot create extra substrate, so the final amount of product must stay the same.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph shows**

Look carefully at the axes. The y-axis is total product formed and the x-axis is time. A steeper curve means a faster rate. A higher final plateau means more total product made.

The solid line is the reaction without added enzyme.

**Apply the enzyme rule**

An enzyme is a biological catalyst. It increases the rate of reaction, so product is made faster at the start.

Crucially, it does not change the amount of substrate available, so the final total product stays exactly the same:
$$rate \ increases, \ final \ yield \ stays \ the \ same$$

**Pick the matching line**

Line A starts steeper than the solid line, so it is faster. It then levels off at the same final height as the solid line, so the total product is unchanged. That is exactly what an enzyme does.

options.A: Correct. It is steeper at the start (faster rate) but plateaus at the same final total as the solid line, which is exactly the effect of an enzyme.
options.B: Incorrect. It finishes higher than the solid line, suggesting more product was made, but an enzyme cannot increase yield beyond the substrate available.
options.C: Incorrect. It starts less steep than the solid line, meaning a slower rate, which is the opposite of adding an enzyme.
options.D: Incorrect. It plateaus much lower than the solid line, meaning less total product, which an enzyme would never cause.
